quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #24
										  					
  

33 Questions • Passing Score 27

questions.question: Railroad crossings should always be considered:

options.text: Safe to cross because trains rarely come.
Dangerous.
Safe places to park your car.
A place where you must stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Dangerous.
questions.explanation: Railroad crossings are always dangerous. Look and listen for trains from both directions. Follow all signs, signals, and flagger directions. Never cross until you are sure it is safe.

questions.question: You may cross double solid yellow lines:

options.text: To pass a slow truck.
To turn into a driveway.
To pass another car.
Never.

questions.correctAnswerText: To turn into a driveway.
questions.explanation: Double solid lines mean you cannot pass or change lanes. You can only cross them to turn left into or out of a driveway, to turn left onto or off a highway, or to make a U-turn where allowed.

questions.question: If an oncoming driver is heading toward you in your lane, you should:

options.text: Honk, steer right, and speed up.
Honk, steer left, and brake.
Honk, steer right, and brake.
Stay centered, honk, and brake.

questions.correctAnswerText: Honk, steer right, and brake.
questions.explanation: First honk your horn to get their attention. If they do not move, steer right to escape. Steering left is dangerous because they might correct at the last moment and you will still crash. Brake firmly and steadily. Slowing down reduces the impact.

questions.question: When you park uphill on a street with a curb:

options.text: Keep the front wheels straight and set the parking brake.
Turn the front wheels away from the curb.
Turn the front wheels toward the curb.
Turn the back wheels into the curb.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn the front wheels away from the curb.
questions.explanation: Turn your wheels sharply left, away from the curb. If your brakes fail, your car will roll away from traffic instead of into it.

questions.question: This road sign means:

options.text: These spaces are reserved for drivers with disabled parking permits.
A roundabout is ahead.
Traffic in this lane must turn in the direction of the arrow.
These lanes are for buses and carpools only.

questions.correctAnswerText: These spaces are reserved for drivers with disabled parking permits.
questions.explanation: This sign marks parking spaces reserved for people with disabled parking permits.

questions.question: Pennant-shaped signs mean:

options.text: School zones.
No passing zones.
Speed limits.
Railroad crossings.

questions.correctAnswerText: No passing zones.
questions.explanation: Pennant-shaped signs show no passing zones. The sign will also have text to confirm it is a no passing zone.

questions.question: When meeting a car with bright headlights, you should:

options.text: Use your bright lights until the other driver dims theirs.
Flash your lights to warn the other driver.
Dim your lights and speed up to pass.
Look toward the right side of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look toward the right side of the road.
questions.explanation: Look away from the headlights and toward the right side of the road until the car passes. This keeps you from being blinded.

questions.question: If you need to slow down on a slippery road, the first thing you should do is:

options.text: Press hard on the brakes.
Take your foot off the gas pedal.
Use the parking brake.
Pump the brakes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Take your foot off the gas pedal.
questions.explanation: First, take your foot off the gas. If you need to slow down more, gently apply steady, light pressure to the brake pedal.

questions.question: This sign means:

options.text: Slippery when wet.
Tow-away zone.
Steep downgrade.
Roadwork ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slippery when wet.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are usually yellow with black markings and prepare drivers for hazards ahead. This sign warns drivers to be careful when the road becomes wet and slippery.

questions.question: At a stop sign, you should stop and:

options.text: Check your rearview mirror for tailgating cars.
Move when the car ahead of you moves.
Look right, then left, then right again.
Look left, then right, then left again.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look left, then right, then left again.
questions.explanation: Look left first because vehicles from the left are closer to you. Then look right, then look left again to check for any vehicles you may have missed.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: The road curves right ahead. Slow down to 35 mph.
A divided highway is starting. Slow down to 35 mph.
Merge ahead. Slow down to 35 mph.
Winding road ahead. Slow down to 35 mph.

questions.correctAnswerText: The road curves right ahead. Slow down to 35 mph.
questions.explanation: This sign warns that the road curves to the right. You should slow down to the safe speed shown (35 mph).

questions.question: To pass a slower vehicle on a two-lane road, you must:

options.text: Not cross the centerline.
Flash your lights at oncoming traffic.
Use the shoulder.
Use the lane for oncoming traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use the lane for oncoming traffic.
questions.explanation: To pass on a two-lane road, you must use the oncoming traffic lane. Only pass if it is safe and legal to do so.

questions.question: How much alcohol does your body process per hour?

options.text: Three drinks per hour.
One drink per hour.
Two drinks per hour.
None of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: One drink per hour.
questions.explanation: Most people's bodies process about one drink per hour. How impaired you become depends on many factors: the amount you drink, how fast you drink, your body weight, whether you have eaten, and your health.

questions.question: Which recommendation does NOT help with safe night driving?

options.text: Keep your windshield clean.
Remember that tinted windows reduce visibility at night.
Keep a flashlight in your vehicle.
Look into the headlights of oncoming vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look into the headlights of oncoming vehicles.
questions.explanation: Looking at oncoming headlights makes your pupils shrink. When the vehicle passes, your eyes need time to adjust back to the darker light. During this time, you cannot see the road clearly.

questions.question: Which factor does NOT affect your vehicle's stopping distance?

options.text: Steering ability
Braking distance
Reaction distance
Perception time

questions.correctAnswerText: Steering ability
questions.explanation: Stopping distance depends on three things: perception time, reaction distance, and braking distance. These change based on your speed and road conditions.

questions.question: When must you pull over for an emergency vehicle?

options.text: No matter which direction it is coming from.
Only if it is behind you.
Only if it is coming toward you.
None of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: No matter which direction it is coming from.
questions.explanation: You must pull over to the right and stop for any emergency vehicle with flashing lights, whether it is behind you or coming toward you.

questions.question: When driving on slippery roads, you should:

options.text: Always drive at the speed limit.
Use cruise control to keep a steady speed.
Follow closer to other vehicles.
Avoid sudden changes in speed or direction.

questions.correctAnswerText: Avoid sudden changes in speed or direction.
questions.explanation: Do not make sudden changes in speed or direction on slippery surfaces. Slow down and do not use cruise control.

questions.question: What does a flashing yellow light mean?

options.text: Stop and look, then go if traffic is clear.
Stop and wait for a green light.
Speed up to cross the intersection quickly.
Slow down and proceed with caution.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and proceed with caution.
questions.explanation: A flashing yellow light means you should slow down and drive carefully through the intersection.

questions.question: If a green turn arrow becomes a solid green light, you:

options.text: Can still turn, but must yield to oncoming traffic.
Cannot turn and must go straight.
Still have the right-of-way to turn.
Do not have to turn in that direction anymore.

questions.correctAnswerText: Can still turn, but must yield to oncoming traffic.
questions.explanation: When a green arrow becomes a solid green light, you can still turn in that direction. However, you must yield to pedestrians and oncoming traffic first.

questions.question: When changing lanes, you should:

options.text: Only use your mirrors.
Start signaling as you move into the next lane.
Signal 500 feet ahead on residential streets.
Always check your blind spot.

questions.correctAnswerText: Always check your blind spot.
questions.explanation: Cars and motorcycles can hide in your blind spot. Look over your shoulder before changing lanes. Signal 100 feet before turning on residential streets or five seconds before changing lanes on a freeway.

questions.question: When entering a highway from an entrance ramp, you should:

options.text: Enter faster than traffic to get ahead.
Enter slowly to avoid other vehicles.
Stop first, then slowly enter traffic.
Speed up to match the traffic speed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Speed up to match the traffic speed.
questions.explanation: Use the acceleration lane to speed up. Signal, look for an opening, speed up to match traffic, and merge safely.

questions.question: If you see this sign, you:

options.text: Cannot pass another vehicle.
Can pass a slow vehicle if you do it quickly.
Can pass if you know the road ahead.
Can pass only at night.

questions.correctAnswerText: Cannot pass another vehicle.
questions.explanation: This is a regulatory sign. You must obey it. This sign means no passing is allowed.

questions.question: Before turning left, it is important to:

options.text: Honk your horn.
Let oncoming vehicles pass first.
Move to the right side of your lane.
Wait for oncoming traffic to get a red light.

questions.correctAnswerText: Let oncoming vehicles pass first.
questions.explanation: When turning left at a traffic signal, you must let pedestrians and oncoming traffic go first.

questions.question: You must let other drivers go first when:

options.text: You are entering a street from a garage or alley.
Another vehicle is on your left and you both reach an unmarked intersection at the same time.
Your traffic signal is a green arrow.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: You are entering a street from a garage or alley.
questions.explanation: You must let other drivers go first when entering from a garage, driveway, or alley. You must also let pedestrians on intersecting sidewalks go first.

questions.question: Your ability to stop is affected by:

options.text: Traffic lights.
Other cars on the road.
The time of day.
How the road surface is.

questions.correctAnswerText: How the road surface is.
questions.explanation: Road conditions greatly affect how fast you can stop. Slow down on wet or slippery roads to keep control of your vehicle.

questions.question: If there is no stop line or crosswalk marked, you should:

options.text: Not stop.
Slow down to check if traffic is clear.
Stop where you can see 200 feet in both directions, even if you enter the intersection.
Stop where you can see oncoming traffic before entering the intersection.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop where you can see oncoming traffic before entering the intersection.
questions.explanation: Stop at the closest point to the intersection where you can see traffic coming. Do not enter the intersection to get a better view.

questions.question: As a pedestrian, you should:

options.text: Always have the right-of-way over vehicles in a crosswalk.
Never cross when vehicles are coming.
Cross anytime because drivers must stop for you.
Use crosswalks only when it is convenient.

questions.correctAnswerText: Never cross when vehicles are coming.
questions.explanation: Do not enter a street or crosswalk if vehicles are approaching. Even though pedestrians have the right-of-way in crosswalks, a close vehicle may not have time to stop.

questions.question: A slow-moving vehicle sign is:

options.text: A rectangular red sign.
A circular green sign.
A diamond-shaped yellow sign.
A triangular orange sign.

questions.correctAnswerText: A triangular orange sign.
questions.explanation: The slow-moving vehicle sign is a reflective orange triangle. Vehicles with this sign are moving at 25 mph or slower.

questions.question: What is a safe way to drive through a curve?

options.text: Slow down as you enter, speed up as you exit.
Keep the same speed throughout the curve.
Speed up as you enter, slow down as you exit.
Stay near the right edge of your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down as you enter, speed up as you exit.
questions.explanation: Slow down when entering a curve and speed up gradually as you exit. Speeding up as you enter makes it harder to control your vehicle.

questions.question: On a highway with two solid yellow lines, you may:

options.text: Cross them only to turn left into an alley, private road, or driveway.
Cross them to pass other vehicles if no traffic is coming.
Never cross them.
Cross them only to make a U-turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: Cross them only to turn left into an alley, private road, or driveway.
questions.explanation: Double solid yellow lines mean no passing in either direction. You may cross them only to turn left into or from an alley, private road, or driveway.

questions.question: What color are the road markings that separate traffic moving in opposite directions?

options.text: Yellow
White
Yellow and white
Yellow, white, and black

questions.correctAnswerText: Yellow
questions.explanation: Yellow lines run down the center of the road. They separate traffic moving in opposite directions.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Heavy traffic ahead
Do not enter
Railroad crossing
Yield

questions.correctAnswerText: Do not enter
questions.explanation: This sign tells you not to enter the road or driveway from your current direction. If you see this sign, turn around and take a different route.

questions.question: Traffic lights sometimes show arrows to control turns from certain lanes. What does a solid red arrow mean?

options.text: It is never used in traffic signals
It means the same thing as a red traffic light
You may turn in the direction the arrow points
Traffic in that direction must stop

questions.correctAnswerText: It means the same thing as a red traffic light
questions.explanation: A solid red arrow means the same as a circular red traffic light. You must stop and cannot turn in the direction the arrow points.
